findings.source_quote: αὐτάς μου τὰς βίβλους, ἃς ἂν μοι δῷ
findings.english_quote: the very books he may give me
findings.issue: The emphasis of αὐτάς is represented, but the possessive μου is not explicitly preserved. Receiving the books does not itself express the source's additional description of them as the speaker's books.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “my books themselves, whichever he may give me.” Review the resulting sentence afresh for both the possessive and the emphatic construction.

findings.english_quote: to a devout and good person undertaking to teach
findings.issue: The source_issues note treats ἐπαναρουμένῳ as morphologically obscure and publication-blocking without recognizing its available analysis as a future-middle participle of ἐπαναίρω. That analysis supports a prospective undertaking to teach. The supplied form is not, merely because it is unfamiliar, evidence of textual corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Reassess the note using the future-middle analysis of ἐπαναίρω and consider “to a devout and good person who will undertake to teach.” Remove the morphology-based publication block unless independent linguistic evidence establishes a genuine problem. Any remaining uncertainty about the verb's contextual force should be recorded as a meaning issue, not a transcription defect. The revised wording and note require fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν.
findings.english_quote: Otherwise, I will not grant the favor of passing this on even to a child or a brother or a friend or anyone who may at any time be related to me in some other way, if he is unworthy, since that would not be proper.
findings.issue: The general exclusion of an unworthy relative is recoverable, but “grant the favor of passing this on” is not securely established by τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν. The draft makes χάριν the favor being granted and τοῦδε the material transmitted, without establishing how that interpretation accounts for the supplied cases and infinitive construction. Its note appropriately acknowledges the difficulty, but acknowledgment does not validate the reconstruction.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep this clause blocked on unresolved syntax and meaning, not on an alleged OCR error. A defensible grammatical account of τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν is needed before the current reconstruction can be approved. If no secure account is available, explicitly mark the unclear construction in the translation rather than presenting “grant the favor” as established. Preserve the supplied reading in source_issues; distinguish any conjectural correction from it. Any replacement must undergo fresh review.

findings.source_quote: εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν
findings.english_quote: But if I do not wish to carry them about with me
findings.issue: The English correctly follows the first-person reference. The source_issues note, however, too readily treats ἑαυτοῦ as a person-agreement irregularity or typographical feature and proposes ἐμαυτοῦ. Greek can use ἑαυτοῦ reflexively with a first-person referent; the construction does not by itself establish a source defect.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the English. Reclassify the supplied ἑαυτοῦ as a disclosed reflexive usage with first-person reference, rather than a demonstrated typographical problem. Remove the proposed correction unless additional linguistic or textual evidence warrants it. Keep this feature separate from the genuinely unresolved opening construction and from the printed punctuation feature παρακαταθήσομαι·,.

findings.issue: “Perhaps” introduces an uncertainty marker not expressed in the Greek. The source says “or even something more,” without that additional qualification.
findings.suggested_revision: Delete “perhaps”: “or even something more.” Review the revised undertaking in its full sentence.

findings.source_quote: πρὸς τούτοις δ’ ἅπασιν εἰ ψεύσομαι, κατάθεμα ἔσομαι ζῶν καὶ θανὼν καὶ αἰωνίῳ κολασθήσομαι κολάσει.
findings.english_quote: Besides all this, if I lie, may I be accursed both alive and dead, and may I be punished with eternal punishment.
findings.issue: ἔσομαι and κολασθήσομαι are future indicatives, whereas the draft turns both into wishes or invocations with “may.” This also erases the source's grammatical distinction from the preceding optative εἴη, correctly rendered “may ... be hostile.” The self-imprecatory setting does not justify making all these verb forms alike.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Besides all this, if I lie, I will be accursed while alive and after death, and I will be punished with eternal punishment.” Preserve the earlier optative separately. Update the lexical note on κατάθεμα ἔσομαι to explain the future assertion rather than endorsing an optative substitution. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Εὐλόγηται ὁ σὲ ὡς πάντα προειδὼς καλῶς ἡμῖν καταστήσας ἐπίσκοπον
findings.english_quote: Blessed be the one who, foreknowing all things, appointed you well as bishop for us.
findings.issue: Εὐλόγηται is a perfect passive indicative. “Blessed be” can make the declaration sound like a wish and substitutes a familiar blessing formula for the supplied verbal assertion. The remainder of the clause is represented.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Blessed is the one who, foreknowing all things, appointed you well as bishop for us,” with a note that the Greek uses a perfect passive expressing the resulting blessed state. Review this replacement afresh. The printed καὶ· αὗται should remain classified as an editorial punctuation feature, not as unresolved textual corruption.
